newsitem.title: EGYPT: Peres says peace process still alive.
newsitem.headline: Peres says peace process still alive.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Shimon Peres said on Sunday the Middle East peace process was not dead and that he was committed to pushing it ahead.

At the seaside resort of Sharm el-Sheikh, the former Israeli prime minister and Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak lunched and held more than two hours of talks on prospects for peace talks, which have snagged on Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.

Peres was defeated in May by Benjamin Netanyahu, ran for the office of prime minister on a platform opposed to trading occupied Arab land for peace and since taking office has lifted restrictions on Jewish settlement in the West Bank.

"I agree completely with what President Mubarak has said that peace is not dead. And personally I do not believe that there is anybody who can kill it," Peres said. "It has a life and a logic of its own and none of us has a better alternative.
"It can be postponed, it can encounter some difficulties, but I am sure that this is the real future and nobody can stop it," he told reporters after his talks with Mubarak.
Peres and slain Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin shared the Nobel prize for the 1993 peace deal with the Palestinians.
Peres last visited the Sinai resort town in March when Egypt and the United States co-sponsored a summit there to support the peace process after a string of deadly bombings in Israel.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have been trying to clinch a Hebron deal in nearly three weeks of U.S.-brokered talks. Netanyahu said this week an agreement was close but accused Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat of procrastinating.
Egypt, which was the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel in 1979, has urged Netanyahu to fulfil the accord the Labour party and Palestine Liberation Organisation signed.

"They (the current Israeli government) have agreed that we have to continue to negotiate. It is not the end of the story -- on Hebron, on the further redeployment, on the permanent solution of the Palestinian issue," Peres said.

Palestinians and Israelis are to continue talks on implementing the accords and the final status of east Jerusalem. Palestinians want the Arab part as the capital of a future state, while Israel calls the entire city its eternal capital.
"There are very difficult issues...but believe me our minds are further than the problems we are facing. And even when we shall sit down I believe there will be new ideas and solutions," Peres said.
"You cannot build a new Middle East with new guns. Believe me it's a catastrophe....let's have a new Middle East basically oriented on the economic development..." Peres said.

Egypt is due to hold a summit in November aimed at integrating Israel into the Middle East economy. But Mubarak has warned Israel that Arab states might make difficulties unless the Jewish state made progress in peace talks.
"I shall not give up the new Middle East. It is the right thing to do," Peres said.
"I'm going to fight for peace in whatever capacity I can, even if I have to be a street cleaner, I shall run in the street and fight for peace."
